findings.passage: "This gives the registrar another tool to be able to clean up those voter rolls, which I will just say, gives a lack of confidence," Kolkhorst told the Senate State Affairs Committee.
findings.note: Dallas Morning News quotes her presenting SB 260 (88R), her bill on voter-registrar address confirmation, in committee. Another story of 2023-04-17 dates the same quote to a hearing 'last month'; the date here is the date of the first story.

findings.passage: There have been some reports concerning voter integrity in some counties. This cannot be tolerated and will not be tolerated. Our team of staff is already looking into every allegation and will work to put even more safeguards in place to ensure that your vote is counted and not discounted by any technocrat or, as my mom used to say, ‘shenanigans!’
findings.note: KBTX quotes her social media statement after the March 2026 primary about reports of voting problems in some counties. It does not mention voter ID or citizenship.

findings.motion: Author of SB 260; engrossed version referred to House Elections 2023-04-20
findings.note: She is the author of SB 260, 'Relating to confirmation of a voter's residence by a voter registrar.' It passed the Senate and was referred to the House Elections committee. It concerns voter-roll address checks, not ID.

findings.motion: Listed as an author (coauthor) of SB 16, proof of citizenship to register to vote
findings.note: She is listed among the Senate authors of SB 16, 'Relating to requiring a person to submit proof of citizenship to register to vote, including the eligibility of certain voters to vote a limited federal ballot if the voter cannot supply the required proof...; creating criminal offenses.' The lead author is Hughes. The date is approximate (bill unveiled in March 2025).

findings.motion: Named as co-author of SB 5 (voter ID declaration changes) in the Attorney General's news release
findings.note: The release says 'The bill is co-authored by state Senators Paul Bettencourt, Brian Birdwell, Dawn Buckingham, Konni Burton, Donna Campbell, Brandon Creighton, Craig Estes, Bob Hall, Kelly Hancock, Don Huffines, Bryan Hughes, Lois Kolkhorst, Jane Nelson, Robert Nichols, Charles Perry, Charles Schwertner, Kel Seliger, Larry Taylor and Van Taylor.' SB 5 adds a declaration route for voters without photo ID and free birth certificates for ID. The release is undated in the text read; the year is from the 2017 session.
subjects: what happens to a voter with no ID

findings.passage: This week I filed two bills that will help preserve the Second Amendment of the U.S. Constitution and protect the liberties of Texas gun-owners. Senate Bill 438 would prohibit the use of public funds to enforce federal and international firearms laws that do not exist under the legislation of Texas. The state government must fight to protect the liberties espoused in the Second Amendment to the U.S. Constitution as the federal government has grossly encroached on those liberties.
findings.note: Her Capitol Hall Report newsletter (Feb 4, 2015) on SB 438, barring state money from enforcing federal gun laws.
subjects: state refuses to enforce federal gun laws

findings.passage: SB 346 would allow Texans' who have a concealed handgun license to carry a handgun openly. Citizens have the right to determine the method of carrying a handgun that is the most suitable for their individual needs, and this bill makes provisions for that.
findings.note: Same newsletter; says she signed on in support of SB 346 (open carry for licence holders).

findings.passage: SB 11 would allow people who hold a concealed handgun license to carry on the campuses of public and private colleges and universities.
findings.note: Same newsletter; says she signed on in support of SB 11 (campus carry).

findings.passage: SB 342 would lift the burdens and barriers on Texans' God-given right to defend themselves and their families.
findings.note: Same newsletter; says she signed on in support of SB 342, which she describes as removing red tape on carrying a handgun for self-defense.

findings.passage: The second bill, SB 439, would protect Texas gun-owners from a deficiency in the current penal code, which criminalizes gun-owners who carry a handgun on another person's property even with that person's permission.
findings.note: Same newsletter; her second filed bill, SB 439, on carrying a handgun on another person's property with permission.
Listed as an author (with two other senators) of SB 438, no public money to enforce certain federal or international firearms laws; referred to State Affairs Feb 9, 2015.
